overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that the trailing path separator check was only needed for POSIX-style roots (e.g., `/`) and did not consider that Windows drive roots (e.g., `C:\`, `D:\`) also have a trailing separator that must be excluded for the directory comparison to work correctly when typing a drive letter.
why_it_breaks: When a user types `Q:\` one character at a time, the intermediate values are `Q:`, `Q:\`, etc. The `hasTrailingPathSeparator` check on line 514 filters out URIs ending with a separator (e.g., `Q:\`) so that the directory comparison uses `dirname(filePickBoxUri)` (which strips the trailing backslash) and compares it against `currentFolder`. Without this check, `resources.extUriIgnorePathCase.isEqual(this.currentFolder, resources.dirname(filePickBoxUri))` evaluates to false for `Q:\` because `dirname(Q:\)` returns an empty path that does not match the expected folder, causing the picker to skip the direct-child navigation shortcut and fail to show matching entries. Pasting the complete path works because the full path bypasses the intermediate single-character typing flow that triggers this logic.

evidence.quote: The simple file dialog updated the path but skipped refreshing contents when navigating from `/` into a child folder.
